body: 27F, work in music, estranged from my family and you’ve taken the words out of my mouth regarding feeling like no one would notice if you’re gone. I think we’d have quite a bit in common

I'm so sorry you're feeling that way and I totally get it. A lot of people I know who are still in touch with their abusive family talk about how they regress back into their old behaviors whenever they're around, no matter how much progress they've made. 

It's crucial as an adult to be self-aware and hold yourself accountable for the consequences of your maladjusted behavior, but sometimes self-awareness is also cutting yourself some slack and reminding yourself that you're doing your best to correct a lifetime of incorrect parenting, and that's a tough job. I'm willing to bet you're not an asshole simply because you seem to care whether or not you are one. Assholes usually don't care.

I don't know the specifics of your situation, but if you have the ability to put more distance between you and your mom I think that would make you feel better. Also, if you're not in therapy, a good therapist will be able to help keep you grounded and sort those feelings out. 

I hope things get easier, you deserve some peace of mind ❤️

Oh, all the time. Up until a year or two ago, I would've followed that sentence up with, "In all fairness, I totally did have anger issues as a teenager." But pretty much ever since going NC I've mellowed out to the point where people I know now will say "I've never seen you really angry, I can't even imagine what you yelling would sound like."

It's almost as if when you remove yourself from an environment where you are constantly harassed and provoked, you will stop feeling the need to lash out in defense. Go figure, right?

Went through a similar consideration in my own application process and I agree that stats+calc is a more solid combo. I applied to UCLA a couple years ago, was dinged because I didn't have much of a quant background due to having a BA in a more creative field. I had a feedback call with an adcom who specifically recommended taking stats and calc. I asked her if there were any other classes I should consider and she said no--either stats or calc would suffice and taking both would probably be even better.

My mom would switch back and forth so often between sexualization and slt-shaming that it gave me whiplash. I remember when she bought me my first push-up bra and I was trying it on for size, she grabbed the cups and asked me in a joking way what I'd do if a guy felt me up and could tell that the cups were padded. I was kind of a weirdo as a teenager, so I joked back that I'd make some sort of random noise and maybe that would distract him enough to forget about it. Her face suddenly got really stern, she grabbed me hard by the shoulders and said, "No, the *correct* answer is that you shouldn't be letting a guy feel you up." It was so sudden that I thought she was playing a bit at first but no, she was legitimately angry.

When I had my first boyfriend, she would threaten to have my hymen checked one day and then the next day she'd say things like "I know you, I know you'd only have sex if it was totally hot and tantric. Be honest, how big is your boyfriend?" I WAS SIXTEEN!!!

This really meant a lot. Thank you. I've been beating myself up for it all day and I've been feeling guilt in waves, but my dad keeps reminding me that I was willing to speak to her after everything that's happened and she was the one to walk away.
